c.tagline: A Belle Époque beach resort on the Basque coast, and the birthplace of European surfing

card: Widely accepted; cash useful for small shops and beach vendors

taxi.fare: Metered, roughly €4 flag fall plus per-km rate
taxi.fareNote: Metered fares are standard and reliable

emergency.note: 112 is the general EU-style emergency number that connects to police, fire, and ambulance

walk: Central Biarritz and its beaches are compact and walkable; surf spots along the Cote des Basques are a scenic coastal walk or short bus ride

safety.safety: Very safe resort town, popular with families and surfers alike
safety.crime: Petty theft on crowded beaches is the main concern

hood_landmark.Grande Plage: The Grande Plage and Hotel du Palais
hood_landmark.Cote des Basques: The Cote des Basques surf beach
hood_landmark.Port Vieux: The sheltered Port Vieux swimming cove

avoid.reason: Watch belongings on Grande Plage and around the beachfront in summer, when opportunistic thefts of unattended bags occur.

hood_desc: The grand main beach lined with the historic Hotel du Palais and casino, the postcard image of Biarritz.
The birthplace of European surfing, with consistent beach breaks and surf schools lining the promenade.
A small, sheltered cove popular with families for calmer swimming than the open Atlantic beaches.
The lively market and shopping district just inland from the beaches, with the best everyday dining options.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink throughout France.

transit.sys: Chronoplus urban bus network (also serves Bayonne and Anglet)
transit.pay: Cash or contactless card on board; rechargeable travel card available
transit.note: Central Biarritz is very walkable; buses connect to Bayonne, Anglet, and the airport

transport.air: Biarritz Pays Basque Airport (BIQ), about 10 min from downtown
transport.train: TGV and regional trains connect via Biarritz-La Negresse station to Bordeaux and Paris
transport.bus: Regional buses connect to San Sebastian, Spain and other Basque coast towns
transport.car: Well connected via the A63 motorway; parking near the beaches fills quickly in summer

net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes
net.ap: An Orange, SFR, or Bouygues tourist SIM or eSIM

tip.s: Not obligatory; rounding up is appreciated for surf instructors and guides
tip.r: Service is included by law; rounding up is a nice gesture, not expected

landmarks: Rocher de la Vierge
An Eiffel-engineered footbridge leads to this wave-battered rock crowned by a white Virgin statue, Biarritz's emblem with sweeping views along the Basque coast.
Grande Plage
The belle-époque heart of Biarritz beach life curves between casino and lighthouse, its striped tents and rolling surf framed by grand ocean-front architecture.
Hôtel du Palais
Built by Napoleon III as a seaside palace for Empress Eugénie, this red-brick imperial landmark still reigns over the Grande Plage as a lavish hotel.
Biarritz Lighthouse (Phare de Biarritz)
Climb 248 steps up the 1834 lighthouse on Cap Hainsart for the definitive panorama over the Basque coastline and the Pyrenees beyond.
Côte des Basques
The cradle of European surfing since 1957, this cliff-backed beach draws longboarders and sunset watchers with views stretching to the Spanish mountains.
Port Vieux (Old Port)
A sheltered cove where whalers once landed their catch, now a charming pocket beach ringed by fishermen's cottages and favored by year-round swimmers.
Aquarium de Biarritz
In an Art Deco building facing the Rocher de la Vierge, seals, sharks and Gulf Stream species animate this classic 1933 marine museum.
Église Sainte-Eugénie
This neo-Gothic church above the Port Vieux, dedicated to Empress Eugénie's patron saint, glows with rose windows and hosts atmospheric evening concerts.
Les Halles de Biarritz
The covered market halls buzz each morning with Basque cheeses, jambon de Bayonne, oysters and gâteau basque, ringed by lively tapas-style counters.
Chapelle Impériale
A jewel-box chapel built for Empress Eugénie in 1864, blending Romano-Byzantine and Hispano-Moorish styles beneath a ceiling of golden bees.

train.note: Biarritz's station, Gare de Biarritz-La Negresse, is about 3 km from the beach and is served by TGV inOui from Paris Montparnasse in around 4h30m plus TER trains along the Bordeaux-Hendaye line. No train crosses the border here: for Spain take the TER to Hendaye, walk across to Irun, and pick up Euskotren's Topo metro to San Sebastian or a Renfe service onward. The through Bordeaux-Madrid and Paris-Madrid sleepers were withdrawn years ago and have not returned. Neighbouring Bayonne, 8 km away, has more frequent long-distance services and is often the better railhead.

bus.note: International coaches stop at Biarritz (Halle d'Iraty) on Rue Chapelet, with a second stop at the airport bus station, rather than at a central terminal. San Sebastian is only about 1h15m by coach and Bilbao around 2h30m, which is far quicker than piecing the trip together by train. Tickets are bought online - there is no staffed counter at the Iraty stop. Local Txik Txak buses (line 816) also run across the border towards San Sebastian for a few euros; carry ID for all cross-border services.

ferry.note: Biarritz has no ferry port - its seafront is open Atlantic surf beach with no harbour capable of taking passenger ships, and neighbouring Bayonne's port handles cargo only. The nearest passenger sailings are Brittany Ferries' Bilbao and Santander crossings to Portsmouth and Plymouth (https://www.brittany-ferries.co.uk/), about 2-4 hours away by coach. Boat trips from Biarritz itself are limited to seasonal coastal excursions and whale-watching cruises.

half.name: San Sebastián
half.blurb: A Basque coastal city known for its curving Concha beach, Belle Époque architecture, and dense concentration of pintxos bars.

half.name: Saint-Jean-de-Luz
half.blurb: A former whaling and fishing port on a sheltered bay, with a historic church where Louis XIV married the Spanish infanta.

half.name: Bayonne
half.blurb: The historic capital of the French Basque Country, its riverside old town known for ham, chocolate, and a Gothic cathedral.

full.name: Bilbao
full.blurb: A Basque industrial city transformed by Frank Gehry's titanium-clad Guggenheim Museum, with a walkable old quarter along the Nervión.

full.name: Col d'Aubisque
full.blurb: A high mountain pass in the Pyrenees near Pau, a classic Tour de France climb with sweeping views over the range.
